headline: Iraq resumes crude exports via Turkish pipeline after 12-year shutdown
summary: Iraq restarted pumping crude oil through a pipeline to Türkiye at an initial capacity of 120,000 barrels per day to bypass Strait of Hormuz transit disruptions.
why: Northern pipeline corridors provide landlocked crude routes from Iraqi oilfields directly to Mediterranean export terminals.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Reopening pipeline export capacity increases alternative crude delivery routes to market.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Restoration of Iraqi pipeline exports to Türkiye increased international supply availability.
